title: USC Merit Scholarships
legacy_titles: USC Merit Scholarship (singular form used in USC statistics)
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission (no separate scholarship application)
funding_type: Tuition remission, partial to full tuition (university-funded)
administering_authority: University of Southern California - Office of Undergraduate Admission
implementing_agency: University of Southern California - Office of Undergraduate Admission (award decisions within admission review; Office of Financial Aid coordinates aid packaging)
programme_action: USC Office of Admission merit scholarship programme; USC states it administers more than a dozen scholarship programmes awarded on academic excellence, leadership, service and talent, and that all international applicants who apply by the appropriate deadline are eligible for USC Merit Scholarships
description: USC Merit Scholarships are undergraduate scholarships administered through the USC Office of Undergraduate Admission and funded from university, private and other sources. USC states that all international applicants who apply by the appropriate deadline are eligible, that there are no minimum eligibility requirements for USC Merit Scholarships, and that awards are made on the basis of a comprehensive, holistic review of academic excellence, leadership, service and talent. USC Merit Scholarships range in value from a few thousand dollars up to full tuition, and USC states that no USC Merit Scholarship covers the full USC cost of attendance. USC does not offer need-based financial aid to international applicants, so a merit scholarship is the principal university-funded gift aid available to international undergraduate students.

award_types: USC Merit Scholarships (Office of Admission; more than a dozen scholarship programmes, ranging from a few thousand dollars up to full tuition)

USC Merit Scholarship for National Merit Finalists (valued at $20,000 per year for admitted students named National Merit Finalists by the National Merit Corporation who list USC as their first-choice institution with NMSC)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: USC administers more than a dozen prestigious scholarship programmes awarded based on academic excellence, leadership, service and talent. Awards made through the Office of Admission range in value from a few thousand dollars up to full tuition and are decided within the admission review. Other USC scholarships are administered by organisations outside the Office of Admission, including academic departments and alumni groups; these generally require a separate application, have varying deadlines and eligibility requirements, may require an interview, and are listed on USC's Scholarship Universe portal.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Not published on the USC pages read for USC Merit Scholarships as a programme. Renewal conditions are set out in each recipient's award notification. USC's financial aid site describes merit scholarships and need-based financial aid as separate processes with separate deadlines.
programme_structure.intake: Annual first-year (fall) entry. The cycle currently published is for the 2027-2028 academic year; USC states its test-optional policy applies to first-year applicants to the 2027-28 academic year.

status_note: USC's first-year admission cycle for the 2027-2028 academic year is the cycle published on the official dates and deadlines page (USC states its test-optional policy applies to first-year applicants to the 2027-28 academic year). Early Decision and Early Action close 2026-11-01; the performing-arts Regular Decision deadline is 2026-12-01; the final first-year Regular Decision deadline is 2027-01-10. Early Decision, Early Action and performing-arts Regular Decision applicants are explicitly considered for USC Merit Scholarships, and USC's international applicants page states that all international applicants who apply by the appropriate deadline are eligible. The next cycle is expected to follow the same recurring pattern (November early rounds, January final first-year deadline); exact 2028-cycle dates should be re-verified when USC publishes them.
verification_type: Official university admission and financial aid pages on usc.edu, plus HTTP verification of official usc.edu image assets
verified_by: Kilo research agent - ScholarZone bachelor's research, slot 35 (USA / USC)
verification_notes: All substantive facts in this record were read directly from official usc.edu pages on 2026-10-03: the USC Merit Scholarships page, the International Students admission page, the first-year Dates and Deadlines page, the Deadline FAQs, the Financial Aid and Scholarships page, the Financial Aid Cost of Attendance page, the Financial Aid International Students page, the Financial Aid Maintaining Your Eligibility page, and the Financial Aid Scholarships page. USC publishes no award named "International Presidential Scholarship" on any page read; that name was checked and is absent from usc.edu, so it is recorded as a removed claim rather than recorded as a USC award.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Common Application opens each August for the following fall entry; USC publishes early-round deadlines of 1 November and a final first-year Regular Decision deadline of 10 January.
application_deadline.application_period: 2027 entry: Early Decision and Early Action - 2026-11-01; Regular Decision for performing-arts majors - 2026-12-01; Regular Decision for all other majors - 2027-01-10. International applicants upload the Financial Statement of Personal or Family Support and English proficiency scores within two weeks of their respective application deadline.
application_deadline.official_rule: USC's Dates and Deadlines page publishes exact calendar dates by round: Early Decision (most majors) - November 1; Early Action (most majors) - November 1; Regular Decision (performing arts majors) - December 1; Regular Decision (most majors) - January 10. Early Decision applicants will be considered for USC Merit Scholarships; Early Action applicants will be considered for USC Merit Scholarships; performing-arts candidates applying by December 1 will be considered for USC Merit Scholarships. USC's international applicants page states that all international applicants who apply by the appropriate deadline are eligible for USC Merit Scholarships. The page does not publish a time of day or a timezone for these deadlines.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The first merit-scholarship deadline of the 2027 cycle is 2026-11-01 for both Early Decision (binding) and Early Action, so an international applicant who wants maximum review time must have the full application, official English test scores and financial documentation ready by late October. USC does not publish a cutoff time of day, so do not assume a late-evening window. Note that Early Decision is binding: if admitted you must enrol at USC and withdraw other applications. International applicants may apply Early Decision.

programme_duration.official_range: Four-year U.S. bachelor's degree structure; USC publishes its cost of attendance for a full-time undergraduate taking 12-18 units each semester over two semesters. USC does not publish a scholarship award term (number of funded years) for USC Merit Scholarships.
programme_duration.renewal_note: Not published. USC Merit Scholarship values are described as annual amounts ("$10,000 per year or more", "a few thousand dollars up to full tuition"), but renewal conditions per year are not published on the pages read and are stated in each recipient's award notification.

funding.scholarship_type: University merit scholarship (gift aid that does not have to be repaid), awarded within the admission decision
funding.monthly_amount_note: USC publishes USC Merit Scholarships as an annual tuition award; no monthly stipend amount is published. Some departmental scholarships administered outside the Office of Admission are disbursed directly to recipients as monthly stipends according to USC's stipend schedule, but those are separate awards with their own applications.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel allowance, installation allowance, insurance or living allowance is published for USC Merit Scholarships. USC's International Students financial aid page lists merit scholarships, on-campus work (excluding Federal Work-Study), limited off-campus work with Office of International Services permission, and private loans with a credit-worthy U.S. citizen or permanent resident co-borrower as the funding routes available to international students.
funding.fully_funded_note: USC states that no USC Merit Scholarship covers the full USC cost of attendance. The 2026-2027 estimated two-semester cost of attendance for a full-time undergraduate on campus is $103,162 (tuition $75,384; fees $1,952; housing $13,510; food $8,442; books and supplies $670; transportation $1,188; personal/miscellaneous $2,016; add a $450 new student fee for the first semester). Off campus the estimate is $102,792 and living with parents or relatives $94,630.

tuition.amount: From a few thousand dollars up to full tuition, per year (USC's published range for USC Merit Scholarships administered through the Office of Admission)
tuition.conditions: Individual amount is determined within the admission review and communicated in the admission offer; it is not published or predictable in advance. USC states that last year over 1,000 admitted students earned scholarships of $10,000 per year or more.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published for USC Merit Scholarships. Departmental scholarships administered outside the Office of Admission may be paid as monthly stipends, but these require separate applications.

visa_support.note: Not published. USC issues the forms required for a student visa after a formal letter of admission, and requires proof of ability to pay tuition and living expenses before doing so. The merit scholarship itself is a tuition award, not visa support.

book_allowance.note: Not published. Books and supplies ($670 for two semesters in the 2026-2027 estimate) are included in the cost of attendance, not in the scholarship.

accommodation_support.note: Not published. Housing and food are components of USC's cost of attendance, not of the merit scholarship.

bond.note: No service or repayment bond is published for USC Merit Scholarships. The only binding commitment described by USC is the Early Decision agreement, which is an admission commitment and not a scholarship bond.

total_estimated_value.note: USC publishes a range rather than a single award value, and states that no USC Merit Scholarship covers the full USC cost of attendance (2026-2027 on-campus estimate $103,162 for two semesters). No total programme value is published, and none is computed here.

coverage: Partial to full tuition remission for admitted undergraduate students (USC's published range: from a few thousand dollars up to full tuition, per year)
coverage_limitations: USC states explicitly that no USC Merit Scholarship covers the full USC cost of attendance; the 2026-2027 estimated on-campus two-semester cost is $103,162.
The individual award amount is not published or predictable in advance; it is set within the admission decision and communicated in the admission offer.

USC does not offer need-based financial aid to international applicants, and federal and university policy limit need-based aid to U.S. citizens, eligible noncitizens, and undocumented students meeting California Dream Act or DACA requirements, so the merit scholarship is the only university gift aid open to international students on this page.

Recipients must still document the ability to finance the full cost of attendance for at least the first academic year at the time of application; USC warns that international applicants may not rely on merit awards to demonstrate their ability to pay.

USC warns that merit selection is highly competitive; 18% of the fall 2024 first-year class received a USC Merit Scholarship and over 1,000 admitted students earned $10,000 per year or more last year, but USC publishes no figure for the number or value of awards to international recipients specifically.

Exact benefit structure, renewal conditions and funded-year count vary by individual award and are not published for USC Merit Scholarships as a programme; some separately administered USC scholarships require a separate application with their own deadlines.

The $20,000-per-year USC scholarship for National Merit Finalists is limited to students named National Merit Finalists by the National Merit Corporation who list USC as their first choice, and is therefore not available to international applicants.
eligible_applicants: International applicants to USC first-year (entering) undergraduate admission, defined by USC as individuals who will enter or have entered the United States with a visa, including applicants already in the U.S. on non-immigrant visas such as E2, H2 or L2

Applicants applying in any USC first-year round who meet the respective deadline (Early Decision 1 November, Early Action 1 November, Regular Decision for performing-arts majors 1 December, Regular Decision for all other majors 10 January)
Transfer applicants to USC are eligible for USC merit consideration through the separate transfer admission process, but transfer applicants may only apply Regular Decision
final_year_condition: For this bachelor's-level award the equivalent requirement is secondary school completion. International applicants must provide official academic records covering the equivalent of U.S. grades 9-12 and be on track to complete, or have already completed, the equivalent of a U.S. high school diploma prior to the start of USC enrolment. Final-year secondary students may apply, must submit external examination results and/or predictions (for example GCSE/IGCSE, predicted IB or A-levels, Indian board examinations, Australian ATAR), and use the Common Application mid-year report or the USC applicant portal to submit fall grades when available.
equivalent_degree_note: USC accepts a range of international qualifications and evaluates each application within the context of the applicant's educational system. The Academic Expectations for International Students page hosts an "International Qualifications" tool setting out USC's expectations for several educational systems; applicants whose curricula are not represented are advised to contact the Office of Admission. USC does not contract with or use educational agents in recruitment and selection.
previous_award_restriction: No restriction on holding a previous scholarship is published for USC Merit Scholarships. USC states only that merit scholarships and need-based financial aid are separate processes, that a student need not submit a need-based application to be considered for an admission merit scholarship, and that separately administered USC scholarships generally require their own application. Some outside scholarships reduce loan or Federal Work-Study components of an aid package rather than university need-based grants.

eligibility.citizenship: No nationality restriction applies to USC Merit Scholarships. USC states that all international applicants who apply by the appropriate deadline are eligible, and that USC Scholarships are administered consistent with the University's Notice of Non-Discrimination, with recipients chosen without regard to race, colour, national origin, sex, sexual orientation or any other prohibited characteristic.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Applicants must provide a valid address outside the United States that is not a P.O. box, even if the current mailing address is in the U.S., and submit a copy of their current passport. International applicants already living in the United States must also submit the financial documents in order to complete their application.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Official academic records from all secondary or senior secondary schools, pre-university programmes, colleges and universities attended, covering the equivalent of U.S. grades 9-12, with completion of the equivalent of a U.S. high school diploma before USC enrolment begins.
eligibility.academic_requirements: There are no minimum eligibility requirements for USC Merit Scholarships. Awards are made on the basis of a comprehensive, holistic review of an applicant's candidacy, weighing academic excellence, leadership, service and talent. Admission itself remains highly selective.
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No minimum GPA or percentage threshold is published for USC Merit Scholarships; USC states there are no minimum eligibility requirements. Programme-level admission expectations for individual educational systems are published in USC's International Qualifications tool.
eligibility.language_requirement: All USC international applicants whose native language is not English, including those already residing in the United States, must submit a USC-approved English proficiency examination to be considered for admission. USC does not grant waivers or exceptions to this policy under any circumstances. Minimums published: TOEFL/TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition 100 with no section below 20 (exams taken before 21 January 2026) or 5 overall with no section below 4 (exams taken on or after 21 January 2026); IELTS or IELTS Indicator 7; C1 Advanced (Cambridge English Qualification) overall 185 or above with 169 or above on each skill; PTE 68; SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing 650; ACT English 27. TOEFL ITP Plus for China is not accepted. Where an official exam cannot be sat, Duolingo English Test 130 is accepted, and applicants admitted with only the Duolingo test must sit the International Student Exam offered through the USC American Language Institute on matriculation.
eligibility.work_experience: Not required and not published as a selection factor for USC Merit Scholarships.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Not formally required, but talent, service and involvement in cultural communities are named as bases on which merit awards are considered.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Not formally required, but leadership is one of the four named bases on which USC Merit Scholarships are awarded.
eligibility.financial_need: Merit scholarships are explicitly not based on financial need. USC does not offer need-based financial aid to international applicants, and federal and university policy limit need-based aid eligibility to U.S. citizens, eligible noncitizens (permanent residents, refugees, asylees), and undocumented students meeting California Dream Act requirements or with DACA status.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Full-time undergraduate enrolment at USC. USC publishes its cost of attendance for a full-time undergraduate taking 12-18 units each semester over two semesters. Awards are made to admitted first-year students at the point of admission; no separate scholarship application or enrolment step exists for USC Merit Scholarships.
eligibility.field_restrictions: No field restriction applies to USC Merit Scholarships as a whole. USC states that awards are also available for students interested in particular fields of study, actively involved in different cultural communities, or living in certain areas of the country. Performing-arts majors (Kaufman School of Dance, School of Dramatic Arts, Thornton School of Music) must apply by the 1 December Regular Decision deadline and carry portfolio or audition requirements; the World Bachelor in Business programme in the Marshall School of Business no longer participates in Regular Decision and requires the 1 November deadline.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: USC publishes no fixed percentage, grade point average or class-rank threshold for USC Merit Scholarships and states that there are no minimum eligibility requirements. Admission expectations are set per educational system through the International Qualifications tool rather than as a single universal number.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Some USC merit programmes and named awards carry their own criteria (for example the $20,000-per-year award for admitted students named National Merit Finalists by the National Merit Corporation who list USC as their first choice with NMSC). Some majors require portfolios, resumes, additional writing samples or auditions. Separately administered departmental and outside scholarships have their own requirements and deadlines.
selection_factors_may_include: Interest in particular fields of study
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: USC states that merit scholarships are not based on financial need and are awarded on the basis of a comprehensive, holistic review of an applicant's candidacy. Selection is described as a highly competitive process.

english_requirement.moi_rule: USC does not publish a medium-of-instruction waiver. USC states that it does not grant waivers or exceptions to the English proficiency requirement under any circumstances.
english_requirement.test_score_note: TOEFL scores use two scales: for an exam taken prior to 21 January 2026 the minimum is 100 with no less than 20 in each section; for an exam taken on or after 21 January 2026 the minimum is 5 overall with no less than 4 on each section. Official scores from approved exams must be submitted within two weeks of the respective application deadline. USC notes that its most competitive applicants score significantly higher: the average TOEFL iBT score for admitted students is above 111, with 25 or higher in each section, and that applicants are admissible below the recommended minimums, although at reduced rates of admission. USC is test-optional for SAT/ACT for the 2027-28 academic year, but international applicants who use the SAT or ACT to demonstrate English proficiency will have those scores assessed for both proficiency and general admission review; the corresponding minimums are 650 on SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing and 27 on the ACT English section.
accepted_tests: TOEFL (including TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition)
Duolingo English Test (only if the applicant cannot sit a USC-approved examination)

language_of_instruction.language_note: All USC undergraduate instruction is in English. Optional English interview supplements (Duolingo, InitialView, Vericant) may be submitted as additional evidence of proficiency; USC states these are used only as an additional tool to assess English-language ability and are not evaluative, and their cost is not covered by the application fee.

application_method.central_application: Common Application (USC's Common Application member ID is 492)
application_method.application_route: Direct application to the University of Southern California through the Common Application. USC Merit Scholarship consideration is automatic with the admission application; USC states that students do not need to submit a need-based financial aid application to be considered for a merit scholarship offered by the Office of Admission.
application_steps: Submit the Common Application (USC member ID 492) by the round deadline: 1 November for Early Decision or Early Action, 1 December for performing-arts majors, 10 January for all other first-year majors.

Optionally submit official SAT or ACT scores sent directly from the testing agencies (USC is test-optional for the 2027-28 academic year; USC school code 4852, ACT code 0470). USC does not accept self-reported scores.

Submit official transcripts of all high school and college coursework completed; international applicants must send official copies of all secondary, pre-university and college records directly from the schools or testing agencies, with a certified English translation where the native language is not English.
Submit one required letter of recommendation from a school counselor or teacher, plus any additional letters required by the intended programme.
Provide portfolios, resumes, additional writing samples or auditions if required by the intended major.
Submit official USC-approved English proficiency test scores within two weeks of the respective application deadline.

International applicants upload the signed Financial Statement of Personal or Family Support, proof of sufficient funds and a passport copy to the USC Applicant Portal within two weeks of their respective application deadline.

Complete the USC Application Affirmations form, which becomes available in the applicant portal after the application is received; the digital signature may be submitted after the application deadline.
Submit mid-year fall grades through the Common Application mid-year report form or the USC applicant portal when available.
Receive the admission decision and any USC Merit Scholarship amount with the offer: Early Decision by mid-December, Early Action in late January, Regular Decision by 1 April.
application_method.application_fee: A Common Application fee applies and a fee waiver may be requested through the Profile section of the Common Application if the fee poses a financial burden; USC does not publish the fee amount on the pages read. The fee does not cover optional English interview supplements.

High school and/or secondary school records should show the equivalent of a U.S. high school diploma on track or complete before USC enrolment.
official_application_documents.document_language: Academic records may be submitted in the native language, but must be accompanied by a certified English translation if the native language is not English.
official_application_documents.document_format: Academic records must be official copies sent directly from the issuing schools or testing agencies. The Financial Statement of Personal or Family Support, proof of funds and passport copy are uploaded to the USC Applicant Portal. The Application Affirmations are completed digitally in the portal.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Official transcripts of all high school and college coursework completed; international applicants provide official copies from every secondary, pre-university and post-secondary institution attended.

selection_process.selection_type: Holistic merit review conducted within the undergraduate admission decision; no separate scholarship application or interview for USC Merit Scholarships
possible_stages: Submission of the Common Application and supporting materials by the round deadline
Holistic review of the candidacy by the Office of Undergraduate Admission, considering academic excellence, leadership, service and talent
Merit scholarship determination within the admission review (no separate scholarship step)
Notification of admission with the scholarship amount: Early Decision by mid-December, Early Action in late January, Regular Decision by 1 April
For admitted international students, subsequent review of financial documentation before a formal letter of admission and visa forms are issued
selection_process.weighting_note: USC publishes no numerical weighting for merit scholarship selection. The stated bases are academic excellence, leadership, service and talent, applied through a comprehensive, holistic review.
selection_process.results_timing: Early Decision applicants are notified by mid-December; Early Action applicants in late January; Regular Decision applicants by 1 April. USC's Deadline FAQs note that students not admitted in an early round are deferred to Regular Decision. Separately administered USC scholarships outside the Office of Admission may require interviews.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: USC publishes no ranking or tier structure for USC Merit Scholarships. USC denotes that awards range from a few thousand dollars up to full tuition and that over 1,000 admitted students earned scholarships of $10,000 per year or more last year.

selection_criteria.additional_factors: Talent (academic, athletic or artistic), interest in particular fields of study, active involvement in cultural communities, and geographic origin. USC states that recipients are chosen without regard to race, colour, national origin, sex, sexual orientation or any other prohibited characteristic, consistent with the University's Notice of Non-Discrimination. USC does not conduct admission interviews and does not track demonstrated interest.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: University of Southern California bachelor's degree (Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Science or school-specific undergraduate degree)
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: 4 years (8 semesters) of full-time study, at 12-18 units per semester
possible_awards: USC bachelor's degree in the admitted major, across USC's undergraduate schools including Dornsife, Viterbi, Marshall, Cinematic Arts, Annenberg, Kaufman, Roski, Architecture, Iovine and Young Academy, Dramatic Arts, Thornton, Price, Rossier, Dworak-Peck and others
degree_outcome.degree_note: The scholarship funds the admitted undergraduate degree; USC does not publish a scholarship-specific award term. USC states that students admitted via Early Decision are expected to enrol in the major chosen on the application.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: USC accepts transfer applicants through a separate process, and transfer applicants may apply only Regular Decision; transfer credit evaluation is handled by the Office of Admission and is not part of the merit scholarship terms.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Recipients receive a tuition credit applied against USC tuition, ranging from a few thousand dollars up to full tuition per year. USC states that no USC Merit Scholarship covers the full USC cost of attendance, and that the 2026-2027 estimated on-campus two-semester cost is $103,162. Tuition is the same for in-state and out-of-state residents.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No fee waiver or reduction tied to the scholarship is published. USC states that an applicant who finds the application fee a burden may request a fee waiver through the Profile section of the Common Application.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Applicants must affirm that the application and all presented work is their own, factually true and honestly presented (USC Application Affirmations). Early Decision applicants must also submit an ED agreement and, if admitted, must enrol at USC and withdraw other applications; failure to do so may result in USC rescinding the admission offer.

application_readiness_checklist: Common Application completed and submitted by the round deadline (1 November for ED/EA, 1 December for performing arts, 10 January for other majors)
School counselor or teacher letter of recommendation secured
Official secondary and any college records requested from issuing institutions early, with certified English translations where required
External examination results and predictions available in advance of the deadline
USC-approved English proficiency test booked early enough for official scores to arrive within two weeks of the deadline
Bank statement or bank letter dated August 2026 or later, and a sponsor letter where applicable, ready to upload within two weeks of the deadline
Passport copy and a valid non-P.O.-box address outside the United States
Portfolio, audition or additional writing materials prepared if the intended major requires them
Realistic funding plan for the full cost of attendance, since no USC Merit Scholarship covers the full cost and no need-based aid is available to international applicants
programme_comparison_fields: Award value range and whether it is tuition-only or includes living costs
Whether a separate scholarship application is required or consideration is automatic with admission
Whether need-based aid is available to international applicants
Deadline structure (single deadline versus early and regular rounds)
English proficiency minimums and whether waivers exist
Whether the institution publishes an average award or a range
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: USC admits and awards on a comprehensive, holistic review and does not require a separate scholarship essay; the Common Application materials, activities and any programme-specific writing are the vehicle for demonstrating academic excellence, leadership, service and talent. Concentrate on a coherent record of sustained academic rigour plus documented leadership or service impact rather than on a list of claims, and address why USC specifically. Applicants should not use financial need as an argument, because merit awards are not need-based and USC offers no need-based aid to international applicants.
profile_fit_labels: Applicant able to self-fund the full cost of attendance
Applicant seeking a partial to full tuition remission
common_mistakes: Assuming USC offers need-based aid to international students; USC states it does not

Treating the merit scholarship as a funding guarantee; USC warns that selection is highly competitive, that no USC Merit Scholarship covers the full cost of attendance, and that applicants may not rely on awards to demonstrate ability to pay
Missing the 1 November Early Decision or Early Action deadline and assuming a later deadline still carries the same weight
Applying Early Decision without understanding it is binding

Submitting bank documents dated before August 2026, or submitting tax returns, mortgages, salary statements, in-principle loans, property valuations, life insurance or retirement accounts, which USC does not typically accept

risk_flags.risk: The scholarship does not cover the full cost of attendance
risk_flags.impact: USC states that no USC Merit Scholarship covers the full USC cost of attendance, and the 2026-2027 on-campus estimate is $103,162 for two semesters, leaving a large gap.
risk_flags.mitigation: Build a funding plan for the full cost from family funds, approved loans with a credit-worthy U.S. citizen or permanent resident co-borrower, on-campus work, and any separately applied-for departmental scholarships on Scholarship Universe.

risk_flags.risk: No need-based financial aid is available to international applicants
risk_flags.impact: Federal and university policy limit need-based aid to U.S. citizens, eligible noncitizens and certain undocumented students, so international students cannot close the funding gap through need-based aid.
risk_flags.mitigation: Verify the bank-verified financial statement (dated August 2026 or later) required at the time of application, and treat any merit award as a reduction rather than the basis of the funding plan.

risk_flags.risk: Award amount is unpredictable and not published per applicant
risk_flags.impact: USC publishes only a range (a few thousand dollars up to full tuition), so the actual award is unknown until the admission offer arrives.
risk_flags.mitigation: Do not commit financially before the offer; request a cost estimate through USC's Calculate Your Costs tools and confirm the enrolment deposit deadline against the award notification.

risk_flags.risk: Early rounds close on 1 November and Early Decision is binding
risk_flags.impact: An applicant who delays to the 10 January Regular Decision deadline has less time, and an Early Decision admit must enrol and withdraw other applications.
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply Early Action rather than Early Decision unless USC is a firm first choice; note that international students may apply Early Decision, and that Regular Decision applicants remain eligible for USC Merit Scholarships under USC's statement that all international applicants who apply by the appropriate deadline are eligible.

risk_flags.risk: English proficiency requirement allows no waivers
risk_flags.impact: USC states it does not grant waivers or exceptions under any circumstances, and official scores are due within two weeks of the application deadline.
risk_flags.mitigation: Book a USC-approved exam (TOEFL, IELTS, C1 Advanced, PTE, SAT EBRW or ACT English) early; aim above the minimums, since the average admitted TOEFL iBT is above 111.

risk_flags.risk: Financial documentation rules are strict and time-bound
risk_flags.impact: Funds must be verified by a bank and dated within the past year (August 2026 or later for the current cycle), and must be uploaded within two weeks of the application deadline; USC issues the formal admission letter and visa forms only after verification.
risk_flags.mitigation: Obtain a bank statement or bank letter early in the correct date window, and avoid tax returns, mortgages, salary statements, in-principle loans, property valuations, life insurance and retirement accounts.

risk_flags.risk: High competitiveness with no published international quota or count
risk_flags.impact: USC reports that 18% of the fall 2024 first-year class received a USC Merit Scholarship but publishes no figure for international recipients, so odds for an international applicant are unknown.
risk_flags.mitigation: Present the strongest available evidence of academic excellence, leadership, service and talent, and hold parallel funding plans for other universities.

risk_flags.risk: Some named USC awards are not open to international applicants
risk_flags.impact: The $20,000-per-year USC scholarship for National Merit Finalists requires National Merit Finalist status, which is not available to international applicants, and separately administered departmental awards may have their own eligibility limits.
risk_flags.mitigation: Focus on the Office of Admission USC Merit Scholarships, for which all international applicants who apply by the appropriate deadline are eligible, and check each departmental award's terms on Scholarship Universe separately.
